starting_principles: Physical constraint on real refracted wave angle: $\theta_2 \in [0, \pi/2]$
Definition of critical condition: threshold of grazing emergence along the interface ($\theta_2 = 90^\circ = \frac{\pi}{2}$ rad)
assumptions: Light propagates from optically denser medium 1 ($n_1 = n_{\text{denser}}$) to optically rarer medium 2 ($n_2 = n_{\text{rarer}}$), satisfying $n_1 > n_2$
Interface between the two dielectric media is flat, smooth, and specular
Media are transparent, homogeneous, and isotropic

ordered_steps.description: Formulate Snell's Law for propagation from optically denser medium $n_1$ to rarer medium $n_2$.
ordered_steps.operation: Isolate the sine of the angle of refraction $\sin\theta_2$
assumptions_applied: Snell's Law validity across smooth dielectric interface

ordered_steps.description: Establish the physical maximum bound of refraction angle in the second medium.
ordered_steps.operation: Set $\theta_2 = 90^\circ = \frac{\pi}{2}$ rad, corresponding to grazing emergence skimming along the interface

ordered_steps.description: Solve for the critical angle of incidence $\theta_c$ corresponding to grazing emergence.
Analyze the wave behavior when the angle of incidence strictly exceeds the critical angle.
assumptions_applied: Conservation of radiant energy at lossless dielectric interface

ordered_steps.description: Generalize the critical angle formula for an optical element immersed in an arbitrary surrounding fluid medium.

applicability_conditions: Light travels from an optically denser medium toward an optically rarer medium ($n_1 > n_2$)
Surrounding medium is non-absorbing and extends at least several optical wavelengths beyond the boundary
